parts.answer: Ammonia has a lower Mr (17) than hydrogen chloride (36.5), so its molecules move faster and diffuse further in the same time.
parts.working: B1 compares Mr (both values or 'lower'); B1 faster diffusion / travels further.

parts.label: d
parts.text: State one safety precaution for this experiment and give a reason.
parts.answer: Use a fume cupboard / wear gloves and goggles; ammonia and hydrogen chloride are toxic/corrosive gases.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Suggest why both pieces of cotton wool must be put into the tube at the same time.
parts.answer: So that both gases start diffusing at the same moment (a fair comparison).

practice.stem: The experiment with ammonia at one end of a long tube is repeated with hydrogen bromide gas, HBr, at the other end instead of hydrogen chloride. [Ar: H = 1, N = 14, Br = 80]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of hydrogen bromide, HBr.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the white solid formed and predict whether it forms nearer the ammonia end or the hydrogen bromide end. Explain your prediction.
parts.answer: Ammonium bromide (NH₄Br); nearer the hydrogen bromide end; NH₃ (Mr 17) diffuses faster than HBr (Mr 81) so it travels further.
parts.working: B1 ammonium bromide; B1 nearer HBr end; B1 reason linked to Mr/speed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The experiment with hydrogen chloride (Mr 36.5) gave a ring 59 cm from the ammonia end in a 100 cm tube. Would the ring with hydrogen bromide be more or less than 59 cm from the ammonia end? Explain.
parts.answer: More than 59 cm; HBr is heavier than HCl so it diffuses even more slowly, and ammonia travels a greater share of the tube before they meet.
parts.working: B1 more; B1 HBr diffuses more slowly than HCl.

practice.stem:
Four identical Petri dishes of jelly (agar) were kept in water baths at different temperatures. A drop of coloured dye was placed in a small hole in the centre of each. The time taken for the colour to reach a circle 15 mm from the hole was recorded.
Temperature/°C: 20, 30, 40, 50
Time/min: 84, 61, 49, 35

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the rate of diffusion, in mm per minute, at 20 °C and at 50 °C. Give your answers to 2 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the relationship between temperature and rate of diffusion shown by the results.
parts.answer: The higher the temperature, the faster the rate of diffusion (shorter time).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain this relationship in terms of particles.
parts.answer: At higher temperature particles have more kinetic energy and move faster, so they spread out more quickly.
parts.working: B1 more kinetic energy; B1 move faster.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest one source of error in this experiment and one way of improving the experiment to reduce it.
parts.answer: Judging exactly when the colour reaches the mark is difficult / temperature of water bath may change. Improvement: repeat and average / use a thermostatically controlled water bath / use a white background.
parts.working: B1 source of error; B1 matching improvement.

practice.stem: A gas jar of air is placed upside down on a gas jar containing a few drops of liquid bromine. The brown vapour takes about 20 minutes to spread evenly through both jars. When the experiment is repeated with the air removed from the jars first, the brown colour fills both jars in less than a second.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why diffusion is much faster in gases than in liquids at the same temperature.
parts.answer: Gas particles are far apart and move quickly with few collisions; liquid particles are close together and keep colliding with neighbours, which slows their spreading.
parts.working: B1 gas particles far apart / move freely; B1 liquid particles close together / more collisions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the brown colour fills the lower jar almost at once when the air has been pumped out first.
parts.answer: There are no air particles for the bromine particles to collide with, so they move in straight lines at high speed and fill the space immediately.
parts.working: B1 no air particles / no collisions; B1 bromine particles travel freely (fast).
